The Tier-1 intersection gate chosen in decision-19 directly addresses (a) and (b) by requiring a Tier-1 health alert before invoking Opus; (c) and (d) stay in their own pipelines and link as calibration context.", "Q2": "60s for `stuck-phase-transition` is too tight for refine — legitimate refiner work on a complex multi-thread issue can take 5–10+ minutes (this pipeline's refine ran 22m total, with one PROPOSED→re-review cycle taking ~5m on its own). Recommended: bump the default to ~180s and/or make the threshold per-phase configurable via PipelineConfig. decisions.question:
Coder needs guidance on the new shared package's name (issue #1962, blocker raised by reviewer_contract).

The plan's TASK-1-5 acceptance reads `from shared.overseer.advisor import consult_advisor` (and similar for the other modules). The implementer placed the package at `shared/egg_overseer/` and imports as `egg_overseer.*` because the existing convention is `egg_*` (matches `egg_orchestrator`, `egg_health`, `egg_agent`, etc.) and because at runtime `/opt/egg-runtime/shared/` is on PYTHONPATH (not its parent), so `from shared.overseer.*` would not resolve in the sandbox.

The reviewer_contract NACK correctly notes that downstream tasks (TASK-7-3, TASK-7-8, TASK-5-1, TASK-8-1) reference the planner's `shared.overseer.*` import path verbatim and will not match the implementation as-is.

Three options:
1. Keep `shared/egg_overseer/` (current implementation), amend the plan/downstream tasks to use `egg_overseer.*` import paths. This matches existing codebase convention.
2. Rename to `shared/overseer/` AND add `shared/__init__.py` to make `shared` a real package, AND update the runtime PYTHONPATH wiring so `from shared.overseer.*` works in the sandbox container.
3. Keep `shared/egg_overseer/` with no plan amendment; treat the planner's `shared.overseer.*` paths as a typo and have the documenter/tester translate at write time.

options.label: Keep shared/egg_overseer/ (recommended) — amend plan to use egg_overseer.* import paths
Rename to shared/overseer/ + add shared/__init__.py + update PYTHONPATH
Keep shared/egg_overseer/ with no amendment; downstream agents translate at write time
Other (explain in reply)

questions.question: Which specific escalation triggers in the overseer today (`sandbox/agent-config/rules/overseer.md:142-153`) need tightening? Please list the concrete false-positive / false-negative patterns you want fixed (e.g., #1722-style stale AGENT_FAILED, long legitimate test runs flagged as stalls, specific 401 patterns that should/shouldn't escalate, etc.).
questions.answer: Concrete false-positive classes to tighten: (a) `agent-heartbeat-stall` fires during legitimate file-reading/research time — observed during this very pipeline at 3.5min into refine while refiner was actively reading source files; (b) `stuck-phase-transition` reads stale contract state from a prior cancelled run and misdiagnoses — observed when the alert claimed 'reviewer silent for 5+min' AFTER the reviewer had already sent a substantive NACK; (c) #1722-style stale `AGENT_FAILED` after phase restart misdiagnosed as deadlock; (d) #1727-style early-exit respawn in fresh pipeline. The Tier-1 intersection gate chosen in decision-19 directly addresses (a) and (b) by requiring a Tier-1 health alert before invoking Opus; (c) and (d) stay in their own pipelines and link as calibration context.

questions.question: Baseline thresholds in `overseer.md` — are any of these values wrong: ~60s for `stuck-phase-transition`, Haiku loop-detection confidence >0.8 across 2 consecutive cycles for `agent-loop`, `overseer_max_cycles_before_re_alert=3`? If so, what should they be and why?
questions.answer: 60s for `stuck-phase-transition` is too tight for refine — legitimate refiner work on a complex multi-thread issue can take 5–10+ minutes (this pipeline's refine ran 22m total, with one PROPOSED→re-review cycle taking ~5m on its own). Recommended: bump the default to ~180s and/or make the threshold per-phase configurable via PipelineConfig. The `agent-loop` Haiku confidence > 0.8 across 2 consecutive cycles is reasonable; leave it. `overseer_max_cycles_before_re_alert=3` is reasonable; leave it.

questions.question: Per-pipeline cap on auto-filed issues — is there a maximum (e.g., 1 per phase, 3 per pipeline) beyond which the overseer should stop filing and escalate via HITL instead? If yes, what cap?
questions.answer: No cap on auto-filed issues. Dedup (decision-6: per-repo search by `agent:overseer` + anomaly-type signature) is sufficient. Don't add a per-pipeline / per-phase numeric cap; it would create another tunable that drifts out of calibration over time.

questions.question: Gateway policy for `gh issue create` from the overseer role — what constraints should the gateway enforce (required labels auto-injected, title/body size limits, rate-limit, allowed repos only, etc.)?
questions.answer: Gateway policy for `gh issue create` from the overseer role: (a) auto-inject required labels (`agent:overseer` + matching priority label) so the overseer cannot omit them; (b) size limits — title ≤120 chars, body ≤50 KB; (d) allowed repos = the pipeline's own repo only (no cross-repo filing). NO rate-limit — drop (c). Dedup + the shadow-mode rollout (decision-11) are the rate-limiting controls.

questions.question: If thread 3 (host→overseer migration) ends up in scope, what must stay in `/sdlc`? The issue says 'report what's going on' and 'manage HITL decisions' — does that include user-facing `AskUserQuestion` options like 'Check agent logs' / 'Nudge agent' / 'Restart pipeline', or do those become overseer-initiated with the host only displaying a passive dashboard + HITL prompts?
questions.answer: /sdlc becomes a thin reporter when host→overseer migration is in scope. /sdlc keeps: (a) surfacing alerts as a passive dashboard, (b) HITL decision handling (`pending_decisions` surfacing), (c) Phase-5 final-handoff prompts. The AskUserQuestion side flows currently in `/sdlc` ('Check agent logs', 'Nudge agent', 'Restart pipeline') become overseer-initiated: the overseer does the diagnostic work and surfaces findings in `OVERSEER_ALERT.detail`, which /sdlc displays. Stall / silent-agent / NACK / long-run / stuck-pipeline-rescue detection logic and the in-memory `{role: {phase, phase_entered_at, …}}` state map all move into the overseer.

questions.question: Success criteria for 'the overseer is now escalating well' — what metric or observable signal counts? E.g., zero repeat same-anomaly alerts per pipeline, >X% of OVERSEER_ALERTs acknowledged by human, auto-filed issues accepted (not closed as invalid) at >Y rate, something else?
questions.answer: Success criteria — a small basket of observable signals: (a) zero repeat same-anomaly alerts per pipeline (dedup works correctly); (b) ≥70% of `OVERSEER_ALERT` messages acknowledged or actioned by the human (not dismissed as noise); (c) of human-approved auto-file recommendations, ≥70% are accepted (not closed as invalid); (d) net reduction in /sdlc HITL prompts per pipeline since the side-flow prompts move out.

questions.question: Any additional constraints or preferences not covered by the decisions above (e.g., GitHub App vs. `gh` CLI for filing, required approvers for auto-filed issues, notification routing beyond Slack, etc.)?
questions.answer: Two additional constraints to bake into the plan: (a) use `gh` CLI via the gateway (not a GitHub App) — matches existing patterns; the gateway already mediates `gh` for refiners and coders, so the overseer role just needs a parallel allow-rule. (b) For the shadow-mode rollout chosen in decision-11, the human's 'should I file this issue?' approval surfaces in /sdlc via the existing `pending_decisions` flow — don't invent a new HITL channel. The advisor returns `recommendation=file_issue` (decision-22), the overseer wraps it in an OVERSEER_ALERT, and the alert flow + a follow-up HITL decision is the path; the existing `provide_input` plumbing handles the rest.
